---
title: "Claude & Claude Code at the School of Medicine"
subtitle: "Hands-on library classes for researchers, clinicians, staff, and students"
---

Two in-person classes from the Cushing/Whitney Medical Library. **Part 1** shows anyone at the School of Medicine how to use the Claude app well and safely. **Part 2** teaches researchers to analyze study data with Claude Code. Both classes use only fictional (synthetic) or public files.

::: {.callout-important title="Data rule: no patient data, ever"}
- In class, use **only the class files and public information**. Never use patient data or other sensitive information in either class.
- **A HIPAA-supported version of Claude is available by request:** `[request link]`. Being HIPAA-supported doesn't approve your project, every feature, or every data set.
- Before you use Claude with real work data, follow `[Yale data classification / policy link]`. Questions go to `[HSIT / HIPAA Privacy Office contact]`.
:::

## The two classes {#classes}

:::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .card .card-body}
### Part 1: Getting started with Claude

Build a Claude Project you'll keep using, then learn to prompt it well and check what it gives you.

**For:** anyone at the School of Medicine. No programming needed.<br>
**Time:** 60 minutes · in person, SHM L 111 · up to 18 people<br>
**AIR track:** Track A Foundations · Beginner

**By the end of class, you'll be able to:**

1. Identify the right tool and settings for your data.
2. Apply prompting patterns to a real task.
3. Evaluate Claude's answers and citations before you use them.
4. Create a Project you can reuse for your own work.

[Class page](part1.qmd) · [Quick reference](part1-reference.qmd) · [Setup](#setup-part1)
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .card .card-body}
### Part 2: Analyzing research data with Claude Code

Take a synthetic clinical trial from raw data to a report with Claude Code in Positron, checking every step yourself.

**For:** researchers, coordinators, analysts, and clinicians who can read a little R or Python. Part 1 helps but isn't required.<br>
**Time:** 90 minutes · in person, SHM L 111 · up to 18 people<br>
**AIR track:** Track C Computational Research · Intermediate

**By the end of class, you'll be able to:**

1. **Configure** a Claude Code project that protects raw and restricted data.
2. **Implement** a plan-first workflow to clean and analyze study data.
3. **Evaluate** AI-generated code and results against the analysis plan.
4. **Build** a reusable command, skill, or hook for a research data task.

[Class page](part2.qmd) · [Slides](part2-slides.qmd) · [Cheat sheet](cheatsheet.qmd) · [Setup](#setup-part2)
:::

::::

**Register:** `[registration link]` (registration required for both classes).

## Start here {#start}

1. **Pick a class** above and register.
2. **Do the setup** before class: [Part 1](#setup-part1) takes about 10 minutes, [Part 2](#setup-part2) about 30.
3. **Read the data rule** at the top of this page.
4. **On class day,** bring your laptop and open the class page. Every prompt has a copy button.
5. **After class,** keep the quick reference or cheat sheet handy, and try the [recommended links](#links).

Part 1 is taught from its class page. Part 2 also has a slide deck: [Part 2 slides](part2-slides.qmd). In the deck, press **F** for full screen and **Esc** for an overview of all slides.

On the Part 2 class page, the collapsed **Instructor notes** boxes hold the instructor's notes. Open them if you're curious, or skip them.
:::

## Setup for Part 1 {#setup-part1}

About 10 minutes. No programming needed.

### 1. Sign in to Claude

- [ ] Get your Yale Claude account: `[sign-up link]`. Do this a few days before class, not on the day.
- [ ] In a web browser, go to **claude.ai**, sign in with your Yale account, and send a test message such as "Hello."
- [ ] Check which version you have. If you're on the **HIPAA-supported version**, some screens may look different (an older layout) and some features may be off. That's fine for class. Ask `[ITS contact]` if you're not sure.

### 2. Choose your practice kit

In class you'll build a Claude **Project**: a workspace with your own instructions and files. Pick one kit. Both use the same steps.

| Kit | Who it's for | What's in it | Download |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Kit A: Article Explainer** (default) | Anyone who reads or explains research articles | A style guide (fictional) and a text copy of an open-access article (Hickey et al., *PLoS Medicine* 2025, CC BY) | [part1-kit-a.zip](downloads/part1-kit-a.zip) |
| **Kit B: Committee Assistant** | Administrative staff who run meetings and committees | A made-up committee charter and meeting notes | [part1-kit-b.zip](downloads/part1-kit-b.zip) |

- [ ] Download your kit's zip file and unzip it somewhere easy to find, such as `Documents`. On Windows, right-click the zip and choose **Extract All**.
- [ ] **Don't upload anything yet.** In class, we'll check your settings first, then build the Project together.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Individual files, and the Windows .md.txt problem"}
**Individual files** (if you'd rather not use a zip):

- Kit A: [explainer-style-guide.md](materials/part1-kits/kit-a/explainer-style-guide.md) · [hickey-2025-telehealth-htn.md](materials/part1-kits/kit-a/hickey-2025-telehealth-htn.md)
- Kit B: [committee-pack-synthetic.md](materials/part1-kits/kit-b/committee-pack-synthetic.md)
- About the kits: [README.md](materials/part1-kits/README.md)

To save a single file, right-click the link and choose **Save link as** (or **Download linked file**). If you just click it, the file may open as text in your browser.

**Windows:** your file may save as `name.md.txt`. That's fine; Claude can read it. To fix the name, open File Explorer, choose **View > Show > File name extensions**, and delete `.txt` from the end.
:::

### 3. Optional: the Claude phone app

Near the end of Part 1 we'll open your Project on a phone. This step is optional; you can do everything on your laptop.

- [ ] Install **Claude** from the App Store (iPhone) or Google Play (Android). Check that the publisher is **Anthropic**.
- [ ] Sign in with the same Yale account.
- [ ] Follow `[mobile device policy]`. Never photograph patient lists, charts, screens, or whiteboards. If you use the HIPAA-supported version, check with `[ITS contact]` before using the phone app.

## Setup for Part 2 {#setup-part2}

About 30 minutes. Do the steps in order. You need a Yale Claude account whose seat includes **Claude Code**: `[how to check / who to ask]`.

### 1. Positron and R (or Python)

[Positron](https://positron.posit.co) is a free data science editor from Posit, the makers of RStudio. It works with R and Python and includes Quarto. VS Code (version 1.94 or later) works too, but class is taught in Positron.

- [ ] Install Positron: <https://positron.posit.co/download.html>
- [ ] Install R or Python and the class packages:

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### R (recommended)

Install **R** from <https://cloud.r-project.org>. Positron finds it automatically. Then, in Positron's **R Console**, run:

```r
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "here", "gtsummary", "gt", "broom", "janitor", "testthat"))
```

#### Python

Install **Python 3.10 or later** from <https://www.python.org/downloads/>. Then, in Positron's **Terminal**, run:

```bash
python3 -m pip install pandas numpy statsmodels matplotlib jupyter pytest
```

In class, you'll swap the project's `CLAUDE.md` for the Python version (the project's `README.md` explains how).
:::

### 2. git (required)

In class, git saves checkpoints of your work so you can undo mistakes.

- [ ] **macOS:** open **Terminal** and run `xcode-select --install`. This installs Apple's Command Line Tools, which include git. If it says they're already installed, you're done.
- [ ] **Windows:** install **Git for Windows** from <https://git-scm.com/downloads>. Accept the default options.
- [ ] Set your name and email. In Positron, open the **Terminal** tab and run:

```bash
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "you@yale.edu"
```

### 3. The Claude Code extension

- [ ] In Positron, open the **Extensions** view (the four-squares icon in the left sidebar).
- [ ] Search for **Claude Code** and install the extension published by **Anthropic**. (Positron gets extensions from the Open VSX registry; VS Code uses its own marketplace.)
- [ ] Open the Claude Code panel and sign in with your Yale Claude account.

### 4. The practice project

- [ ] Download [hypertension-cohort.zip](downloads/hypertension-cohort.zip). It holds a synthetic blood-pressure trial, a data dictionary, an analysis plan, REDCap-style exports, and legacy SAS/Stata code.
- [ ] Unzip it somewhere easy to find, such as `Documents`.
- [ ] In Positron, choose **File > Open Folder** and select the `hypertension-cohort` folder.

### 5. Check that it works

- [ ] In the Claude Code panel, send this prompt:

```text
Read the README and CLAUDE.md, then tell me in three sentences what this project is.
```

- [ ] Type `/status` in the panel. Check that it shows your Yale account. Note the version number.

If Claude describes a synthetic hypertension trial, you're ready.

| Extra | Why | How |
|---|---|---|
| **Standalone Claude Code CLI** | A few things in class only work in the terminal version. You can also just watch those parts. The extension doesn't add `claude` to your Terminal. | `[link to current install instructions]` (see the [Claude Code docs](https://code.claude.com/docs)) |
| **jq** | To try the hook example yourself | macOS: `brew install jq` · Linux: `sudo apt-get install jq` · Windows: `[local guidance for Windows users]` (the sandbox needs WSL2) |
| **Claude phone app** | To watch and approve your laptop's Claude Code session from your phone with `/rc` (Remote Control), if enabled. Remote Control is off in the HIPAA-supported version. | Install **Claude** by Anthropic from the App Store or Google Play and sign in. Follow `[mobile device policy]`. |

- [ ] Read the institutional AI and data policy: `[link to institutional AI and data policy]`.

### Trouble?

| Problem | Try this |
|---|---|
| Can't sign in to Claude | Confirm your sign-up went through: `[ITS / help contact]` |
| The Claude Code extension doesn't show up in Positron's Extensions view | Search for "Claude Code" by Anthropic, update Positron, or try VS Code. In class, pair with a neighbor or watch the instructor's screen. (Claude Code on the web, at claude.ai/code, is a different product that runs cloud sessions on GitHub repos. It isn't a stand-in for this class.) |
| "Claude Code isn't included in your plan" | Your seat may not include Claude Code: `[who to ask]`. In class, pair with a neighbor or watch the instructor's screen. |
| `git` isn't found | Finish the git step above, then close and reopen Positron. |
| R or Python packages won't install | Bring the error to class, or come early: `[office hours link]` |

## Access and alternatives {#access}

| If… | Do this |
|---|---|
| **You don't have a working Claude account** | Request one at `[sign-up link]` before class. In class, pair up with someone who has one. Don't create a personal Claude account for anything except the public class files. |
| **Your primary appointment is with YNHHS** | Use the chat AI that YNHHS approves: `[approved tool, e.g. Microsoft Copilot: link, confirmed by ___ on DATE]`. Yale's Clarity may not be available to you `[confirm]`. In Part 1, follow the [Copilot path](part1-reference.qmd#copilot) with the same kits. |
| **You use the HIPAA-supported version of Claude** | Your screens may look different and some features (such as skills, Cowork, and `/rc`) may be off. Check with `[ITS contact]`. |
| **You don't have a smartphone** | No problem. The phone step in Part 1 is optional, and you'll do the same work on your laptop. |
| **Your Claude seat doesn't include Claude Code** (Part 2) | Pair with a neighbor or watch the instructor's screen. Ask `[who to ask]` about access. |
| **You need an accessibility accommodation** | Contact `[accessibility contact]` before class. |
